title: Binary Search
keyIdea: Sorted array → look at the middle. If it's too small, the target can only be to the right; too big, only to the left. Throw away half each step: O(log n).

approaches.name: Linear scan
approaches.idea: Check every number from left to right until you find the target.
approaches.why: Up to n checks. Works, but ignores that the array is sorted, and the problem explicitly asks for O(log n).

approaches.name: Binary search
approaches.idea: Keep s and e around the part that could still hold the target. mid = s + (e − s) / 2. Equal → return mid. Too small → s = mid + 1. Too big → e = mid − 1. s > e → return −1.
approaches.why: Each look halves what's left, so after k looks about n / 2ᵏ remain. That hits 1 after log₂ n looks: ~14 for 10⁴ numbers.

quiz.q: Why mid = s + (e − s) / 2 instead of (s + e) / 2?
options: s + e can overflow int when both are large; e − s can't
It rounds up instead of down

quiz.q: nums[mid] < target. What's the next step?
options: s = mid + 1: mid and everything left of it are too small

quiz.q: Why is the loop condition s <= e and not s < e?
options: When s == e there's still one number left to check

quiz.q: About how many looks for 1,000,000 numbers?

steps: Is the array sorted? Can there be duplicates? What do you return if the target is missing?
